subject: Post-demo: noise containment & recommended deployment pathway for Medsure
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsure.com>, ops+procurement@medsure.com
Cc: security@medsure.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: noise containment & recommended deployment pathway for Medsure

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Short recap and the asks we promised to follow up with.

TL;DR: Based on your traffic profile and p95 latency target, we recommend a Dedicated baseline PoC with guardrails for isolation + an ops playbook for fallback to hosted variants. Details below.

What we covered in the demo
- Inference patterns: many short requests (avg tokens 18) with spikes during claims batch processing windows (observed 30–60% of daily traffic concentrated in 2 hours).
- Sensitivity: PHI in inputs; retention/segmentation requirements noted by your security team.
- SLO goals: your infra team mentioned p95 generation < 300ms for single-turn responses.

Your stated concerns
- Noisy neighbor effects during spikes causing latency regressions.
- Predictability for SLAs during peak jobs and audit/logging for compliance.
- Cost/contract tradeoffs between hosted API and reserved Dedicated capacity.

Our recommended next steps
1) Technical PoC on a Dedicated pool (2 GPU-equivalent baseline) for a 2-week window to characterize tail latency under your peak windows. We’ll instrument token-level tracing, KV-cache warmups, and continuous batching configs. (Attachment: medsure-mvp-load-profile.csv)
2) Isolation guardrails doc from Redwood (attached: isolation-guardrails-checklist.docx) mapping what we can guarantee in Dedicated vs Private VPC.
3) Security evidence handoff: we’ll share the SOC/Security summary and work with your security@medsure.com to confirm data flows and KMS options.
4) Commercial: Ben (cc’d) will put together a short Dedicated pricing sketch + a hosted fallback quote if you want to mix modes.

Concrete asks for you
- Can you share exact p95/p99 targets for both user-facing latency and batch job SLAs?
- Confirm the peak window(s) and an expected QPS during those windows (ballpark is OK).
- Any procurement timelines we should be aware of?

Attachments: redwood-tenancy-options-v2.pdf, medsure-mvp-load-profile.csv

Best,
Lauren
Senior Solutions Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsure.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+procurement@medsure.com, security@medsure.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: noise containment & recommended deployment pathway for Medsure

Hi Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers and follow-ups from our side.

Targets and traffic
- p95 target: 300ms for interactive claims lookups; p99 target: 700ms. Batch job window (ETL-style enrichments) tolerates up to 2s, but anything above 3s triggers retries and backpressure in our pipeline.
- Peak QPS estimate during daily run: ~110 qps sustained for 20–30 minutes; occasional bursts to 200 qps for 2–3 minutes. Typical non-peak is 6–12 qps.

Questions for Redwood
1) If we start Hosted API, how often do noisy-neighbor latency spikes happen in practice for workloads like this? Do you have quantified tail-latency percentiles for hosting multi-tenant for models similar to the Llama-3-class examples?
2) With Dedicated, what isolation guarantees do we get? Specifically: network-level co-tenancy, GPU sharing, and preemption behavior.
3) If we go Dedicated for production, can we keep a small hosted fallback policy (cheaper model) automatically in case our pool is degraded? How is rolling failover handled from a routing/consistency perspective?
4) Timeline: procurement expects an internal review next Wed (2027-05-11). If we can get a scoped PoC plan + rough cost, that will help.

Security (from security@medsure.com)
- We need KMS options confirmed (customer-managed preferred), proof of audit-logging for inference events, and a basic data residency statement.

Thanks — Samir
VP, Platform Engineering
Medsure Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsure.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: noise containment & recommended deployment pathway for Medsure — internal ask

Ben / Stephanie — looping you in with Samir's answers above. Two immediate asks so we can respond before Medsure’s review on 2027-05-11.

1) Ben: please draft a short Dedicated PoC plan (one-pager) that covers the following by EOD Wed 2027-05-05:
   - Baseline config: how many GPU equivalents to recommend for sustained 110 qps with burst headroom to 200 qps.
   - Expected p95/p99 under that config (ballpark numbers based on previous customers and internal perf tests).
   - Isolation guarantees: what we can promise about GPU exclusivity, preemption, noisy neighbor mitigation (kernel isolation, scheduling), and whether we offer CPU-network isolation on the host.

2) Stephanie: prepare a short security appendix (two paragraphs) that confirms KMS/CMEK options, audit logging retention, and data residency options (US regions). Also include the standard SOC/Security doc links.

Also note Samir's fallback question: we should document a routing policy that will failover to a hosted, smaller-capacity model automatically and how we preserve consistency (e.g., model variant pinning + request metadata preserved). Ben — include the ops playbook steps for that failover.

I’ll draft the commercial sketch after Ben posts the PoC spec. Goal: deliver PoC plan + cost sketch to Medsure by EOD Thu 2027-05-06 so they can prepare for their next-week review.

Thanks — Lauren

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsure.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: noise containment & recommended deployment pathway for Medsure

Samir — hi, Ben here (solutions engineering). Quick, pragmatic plan below; attaching the Dedicated sketch and a short failover playbook.

Suggested PoC (2-week) — Dedicated baseline- Config: 2 x A10s-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) with autoscale headroom for bursts up to 3x for 3–5 minutes via burst capacity.- Why: 2 GPU-equivalents give predictable KV-cache residency for your typical 18-token payloads and sustain ~120 qps with p95 ≈ 220–280ms in our benchmarks for similar models; p99 expected ~600–800ms under heavy burst if batching is tuned.- Isolation: Dedicated pools provide the following guarantees:
   • No GPU-sharing with other tenants (customer-dedicated GPU assignment).
   • Scheduler-level reservations to prevent preemption during reserved windows; burst capacity uses preemptible nodes with clearly documented degradation behavior.
   • Network isolation at VPC level when configured (for Private deployments we can offer additional NIC-level controls).

Fallback behavior- We will configure an automated routing policy: primary -> Dedicated pool (pinned model); fallback -> Hosted variant (smaller quantized model). Requests routed to fallback preserve metadata and are tagged so retries/alerts are generated. Failover is tested via canary and a circuit-breaker that trips based on configurable latency/health metrics.

Security notes (summary)- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) in our US regions.- Audit logs: token-level events and request traces stored for 90 days by default (longer retention available as add-on).- Data residency: Hosted & Dedicated in our US region; Private on-prem options available if you need strict regional isolation.

Next steps / delivery timeline- By Thu 2027-05-06 EOD: commercial sketch (monthly avg committed vs burst pricing) + PoC runbook (how we’ll run the 2-week soak and which metrics we’ll capture).- We’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with your infra + security teams to align instrumentation and test traffic shape.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pocexplain.pdf, failover-playbook.txt

Looking forward to the kickoff — Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
